newsitem.title: UK: Soft oils firm, palm little changed in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Soft oils firm, palm little changed in Europe.

text.p: Soft oils remained firm at London's midday on Thursday on the European vegetable oil market with sellers as much as two guilders per 100 kilos up.
A strong dollar against European currencies and higher Chicago futures on weather concerns supported prices.
Dutch soy oil sellers were two to one guilder up while rape oil was 0.75 to 1.50 guilders higher.
However, so far buyers have been reluctant to move ahead of the USDA crop report due later on Thursday.
Coconut oil was fully steady with sellers $7.50 up while palmkernel oil was $7.50 to $2.50 higher.
Traders said the increase was mainly due to the local holiday in the Philippines and doubted there would be much interest.

Palm oil prices were mixed but movements were minimal with the market expected to remain quiet ahead of the Wong report due for release on Friday and the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority official output, stocks and export data expected on Monday.
Malaysian plantation houses estimated an increase in May palm oil output at between four and 10 percent on Thursday.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged after Jun traded at $542.50 a tonne cif.
RBD palm oil offers were $2.50 up in a tradeless market while olein was $2.50 down after Aug/Sep traded at $552.50 a tonne Malaysian ports.
